coverage: Read all 24 criteria and both same-matter prompts; reviewed pertinent portions of the accumulated motion, complaint, Bradbury, Guerine, and Langenhorst materials and relevant statistical-report pages. Confirmed that assignment-2 extracted attachments duplicate assignment-1 contents apart from source headers, and that only defense affidavits are in the motion. The full statistical volume was searched and relevant cited pages read, not reviewed page by page. No proposed or executed plaintiff-side affidavit is in the supplied packet, and no solver call was made.

findings.title: Five physician affidavits are required but absent from the permitted packet
findings.explanation: Sequential dependency: assignment 1 asks the lawyer to review a motion and the rubric suggests obtaining the five doctors' affidavits; assignment 2 then asks to include affidavits referenced from assignment 1. The supplied source material provides the names and a supervisor's collective report that the doctors would find DuPage inconvenient, but contains no individual sworn or signed statements. Criteria 1-10 demand that the response be supported by five specific affidavits and attribute an inconvenience declaration to each. A careful litigator could prepare proposed declaration forms for each doctor, identify the supervisor's reported conversations, and request execution, but could not truthfully represent the brief as already supported by five affidavits. The criteria fail that careful response and reward fabricated filed evidence.

evidence.quote: Please include all affidavits and information you referenced from Assignment #1.
The names of the physicians from Cook County we have spoken to are:

They have advised me that they are all Cook County residents and are willing to testify, however, it would be inconvenient for them to take time away from their practice/at the hospital to testify in DuPage rather than Cook County.
the response is supported by the affidavit of Liam Vance
the affidavit by Liam Vance indicates that DuPage County would be an inconvenient forum for him

findings.suggested_fix: Accept a response using the five doctors' reported positions with proposed, explicitly unexecuted declarations for verification, or supply actual executed affidavits before grading the brief as supported by them.

findings.title: Sara's affidavit and personal inconvenience are invented by the rubric
findings.explanation: The packet says Sara resides in Kane County, but says nothing about her own travel, scheduling, or litigation burden in DuPage. It supplies no affidavit from her. A careful lawyer can ask Sara whether DuPage is inconvenient and draft a proposed affidavit if she confirms it, but cannot truthfully assert that her sworn statement already supports the response or says DuPage would be inconvenient. These criteria give credit for an unsupported factual representation and fail a source-faithful brief that identifies the need for client confirmation.

evidence.quote: By way of background, our client, Sara Davis, resides in Kane County, Illinois.
the response is supported by the affidavit of the plaintiff, Sara Davis.
the affidavit by the Plaintiff, Sara Davis, indicates that DuPage County would be an inconvenient forum for her

findings.suggested_fix: Remove the signed-affidavit requirement unless Sara's statement is supplied; credit a proposed affidavit conditioned on Sara verifying personal inconvenience.

findings.title: Penalty for a true clearance rate in a candid response
findings.explanation: Penalty misfire: the criterion deducts for stating the report's true 60.5% all-case Cook County clearance rate. The motion relies heavily on that figure; a careful response may concede it accurately and explain that this civil case is better compared using civil-category rates, 97.9% for Cook and 96.3% for DuPage, with no comparable Cook time-to-verdict datum. The same rubric rewards the civil figures in criteria 19 and 20. Merely stating the true adverse number does not make the response wrong; the defect is using it as an unqualified measure of likely civil-case speed.

evidence.quote: States in Assignment #2 that the 2023 Illinois Annual Report Statistics report a 60.5% clearance rate in Cook County, Illinois.
was 60.5%, compared to 99.0% in the 18th Judicial Circuit

findings.suggested_fix: Penalize reliance on the all-case clearance rate without civil-case context, while allowing an accurate concession that distinguishes it from the relevant civil data.
